summary.text: Don Coover, a Democratic veterinarian and rancher, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Kansas's 2nd Congressional District to Derek Schmidt.
A first-time candidate raised on a small dairy farm in rural southeast Kansas, he is a West Point graduate who served about ten years in the U.S. Army.

paragraphs.text: Coover was born and raised in rural southeast Kansas, the second oldest of seven children in a family that ran a small dairy, alfalfa, and soybean farm. According to his campaign website, his father was a union truck driver and farmer and his mother a school teacher.
He earned a bachelor's degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, where, according to his campaign website, he was on the intercollegiate pistol team and was an intramural boxer.
He served in the U.S. Army for about ten years; in his Ballotpedia survey, he says he was a military intelligence officer and pilot and rose to the rank of Captain.

Coover earned a graduate veterinary degree from Kansas State University's School of Veterinary Medicine. In his Ballotpedia survey, he says he runs a beef genetics company providing reproductive technologies for cattle, sheep, and goats, as well as a cattle ranch and a veterinary practice serving local and regional livestock producers.

He advanced from the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for the 2nd District. He describes himself as a first-time candidate, and his campaign site says he was running in part for the future of his granddaughter.
During the campaign, he emphasized affordability, rural hospital closures, opposition to tariffs, and getting people with working-class backgrounds into Congress.
He received 45% of the vote to Derek Schmidt's 51.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
